identity.name: People's Republic of China
native_names: 中华人民共和国 (Zhōnghuá Rénmín Gònghéguó)

land.text: the communist-held land at the proclamation: north and northeast China, Shandong, Henan, Shanxi, the lower Yangtze to Nanjing

predecessors.note: The Communist state and party become the People's Republic on 1 October 1949 (Chinese Civil War page).

land.text: the mainland south and west of the communist-held land of 1 October 1949: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Yunnan, Guizhou, Xinjiang, Qinghai and the rest

predecessors.note: The mainland the Republic lost between October 1949 and April 1950 (Guangzhou, Chongqing, Chengdu, then Hainan). The Republic continues on Taiwan and its islands (the China page: it 'retreated to Taiwan and continued to claim legitimacy').

capitals.name: Beijing (Beiping)
capitals.note: Infobox capital: Beijing. The Chinese Civil War page: Mao Zedong proclaimed the PRC 'with its capital at Beiping' on 1 October 1949; the pages opened do not date the renaming.

correction.text: the mainland at the end of 1949: the communist-held land of 1 October 1949 (Communist Party of China, 2,785,265 km2) plus the Guangzhou, Chongqing, Chengdu and southwest, northwest and southern gains of October-December 1949, i.e. Cliopatria's 1950 outline, which contains the 1949 Communist outline; the compiler compares a keyframe with the ledger at the end of its start year

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's People's Republic begins in 1950 but Mao Zedong proclaimed it on 1 October 1949. The shape of the day is the Communist Party of China's 1949 outline (2,785,265 km2); Cliopatria's 1950 shape (8,412,473 km2, the mainland less Tibet and Hainan) is reached by the October-December 1949 gains in the ledger. [fx-21 2026-11-01: the correction was the 1 October shape alone (14,096 cells), but ledger /1 to /4 (Guangzhou, Chongqing, Chengdu and the rest of the mainland, 'placed at the year's end') lift the state to 34,019 cells before the keyframe is compared at the end of 1949, so the compiler released 19,925 cells (Xinjiang 4,583, Qinghai 2,673, Sichuan 1,893, Gansu 1,687, Yunnan 1,385, Inner Mongolia 1,127 ...) and the 1950 keyframe added 20,379 back. The keyframe is now the end-of-1949 shape. Chinese Civil War page: 'the majority of the resistance collapsed after the fall of Chengdu on 10 December 1949', 'the Kuomintang retreat to Taiwan on 7 December 1949', and by late 1949 'only Tibet was left'. The page dates no Xinjiang, Qinghai, Gansu or Yunnan takeover. Left alone: Cliopatria's 1950 outline also carries Chamdo (991 cells of Xizang), which the PLA took in October 1950 (ledger /6), so the state holds it from December 1949 here and in the ledger.]

correction.text: the mainland of 1950 (Chamdo already inside, Hainan added); holds 1950 only, 1951-1952 is the new keyframe

keyframe_review.note: 8,412,473 km2 for 1950-1952. It has no cell of Hainan, which the page dates to 'the Communist conquest of Hainan Island in April 1950'; it holds 991 cells of Xizang (the eastern part with Chamdo and Qamdo, taken in October 1950) and none of central Tibet (Lhasa, Shigatse), which came 'under Chinese control' with the 1951 agreement (Annexation of Tibet infobox). The infobox area of 9,596,961 km2 (China page, present day) is 1.14 times this shape and 1.025 times the 1953 one; the 1950-1953 gap is Tibet (3,591 added cells, about 1.0 M km2, with Hainan's 125 cells) as Cliopatria draws it.

union.text: U-Tsang (central Tibet), the land of the Seventeen Point Agreement

correction.text: the 1950 mainland, Hainan and U-Tsang: Cliopatria's 1953 shape reached two years early

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Seventeen Point Agreement was signed on 23 May 1951 and the Dalai Lama 'formally accepted' it in October 1951 (infobox ends 24 October 1951: 'U-Tsang and the Chamdo Region of Kham came under Chinese control'), yet Cliopatria keeps a separate Tibet shape to 1952 and gives the PRC the land only in 1953. The page is silent on the PLA's entry into Lhasa ('Shortly afterwards, the PLA entered Lhasa'). Hainan is included from April 1950.

9,360,791 km2 with Tibet and Hainan inside and Taiwan outside (the page: 'The PRC claims the ROC's territory, most of which is under the claimed Taiwan Province', governed by the Republic of China). The infobox gives 9,596,961 km2 today; ratio 0.975.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid for 1956 only: the next keyframe adds Aksai Chin from 1957

keyframe_review.note: 9,360,900 km2, one cell more than 1953. The page says 'In 1956-57, China constructed a road through Aksai Chin, connecting Xinjiang and Tibet', and that after the 1962 war China 'continued its de facto control of the Aksai Chin' (infobox: 'Status quo ante bellum'): the war moved no border, so Cliopatria's 1963 addition of about 27,000 km2 (108 cells) comes years too late.

union.text: Aksai Chin, the plateau crossed by the Xinjiang-Tibet road

correction.text: the 1956 shape plus Aksai Chin, held de facto from the road of 1956-57

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Aksai Chin (about 27,000 km2 in the gazetteer's cells; the 1963 shape adds about 32,000 km2 in all) is drawn as Chinese from 1957, the road's year; India claims it, and the 1962 war ended 'status quo ante bellum'. The page does not date China's first control and does not give Aksai Chin's area (it is 'an area the size of Switzerland'), so the year is a reading of the road, confidence 2.

9,395,781 km2: the 1957 shape plus a strip on the Karakoram watershed (the page mentions 'a 1963 China-Pakistan Border Treaty', which concerned the Pakistan-controlled Kashmir boundary). No page opened dates the strip.

9,395,480 km2: one cell more and two fewer, all near 78 E 36 N on the Karakoram, i.e. rasterisation of the same border. The China page says the PRC has had 23 border disputes since 1949, six of them unsettled (closely paraphrased), and gives 14 land neighbours and 22,117 km of land border; no treaty is dated on it (Burma, Nepal, Mongolia, Soviet Union: unverified, page budget).

correction.text: unchanged shape for 1992-1996; Hong Kong joins in 1997 and Macau in 1999

keyframe_review.note: 9,395,623 km2: two more and three fewer cells than 1987 on the Tajik, Kazakh and Kyrgyz frontiers, too small to date. It lacks Hong Kong (1,104.4 km2) and Macau (31.3 km2), which the page says were 'transferred to China in 1997 and 1999 respectively'; Cliopatria adds four cells in 2000.
New keyframe: Hong Kong, transferred in 1997 (the page gives no day).

correction.text: the 1992 shape plus Hong Kong and Macau, i.e. Cliopatria's 2000 shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Macau, transferred in 1999 (the page gives no day). The shape equals Cliopatria's 2000 outline.
9,399,444 km2 against the infobox's 9,596,961 km2: ratio 0.98. Taiwan, which the Republic of China governs, is outside.

region.text: the communist-held land of the day

ledger.note: 1 October 1949: Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic of China, capital at Beiping (Beijing). Infobox 'Proclamation of the People's Republic: 1 October 1949'; the Chinese Civil War page: 'Mao Zedong officially proclaimed the People's Republic of China (PRC) with its capital at Beiping'. The page names no territory; the Communist Party of China's 1949 outline is the reading.

region.text: Canton, the Nationalist seat until 15 October

ledger.note: October 1949: Guangzhou passes to the Communists. 'The KMT government retreated to Canton (Guangzhou) until 15 October'; the page does not say who took the city or on what day.

region.text: Chongqing, the Nationalist seat until 25 November

ledger.note: November 1949: Chongqing falls. The Nationalist government stayed 'in Chongqing until 25 November'; the page does not date the capture.

region.text: Chengdu, the last Nationalist stand on the mainland

ledger.note: 10 December 1949: Chengdu falls and resistance collapses. 'The majority of the resistance collapsed after the fall of Chengdu on 10 December 1949.'

region.text: the mainland south and west of the communist-held land of 1 October 1949: Guangdong, Guangxi, Sichuan, Yunnan, Guizhou, Xinjiang, Qinghai and the rest

ledger.note: December 1949: the rest of the mainland is Communist. The page dates the Nationalist retreat to Taiwan to 7 December 1949 and the collapse of resistance to the fall of Chengdu (10 December), but not Xinjiang, Qinghai, Yunnan, Guizhou or the other provinces; the outline is Cliopatria's 1950 shape less the 1949 Communist land, placed at the year's end.
April 1950: Hainan falls to the People's Liberation Army. The page: 'the Communist conquest of Hainan Island in April 1950'.

region.text: the Chamdo Region, the western part of Kham

ledger.note: 7 October 1950: the PLA enters eastern Tibet and takes Chamdo. 'On 7 October 1950, Chinese troops advanced into eastern Tibet, crossing the border at five places' (the Jinsha 'on 6 or 7 October'); Chamdo was captured 'by 19 October' and 'the Quamdo battle thus came to a victorious end on October 24'.

region.text: the Chamdo Region, the western part of Kham

ledger.note: 23 May 1951: Chamdo's occupation ends in annexation under the Seventeen Point Agreement. 'Tibetan representatives in Beijing and the PRC Government signed the Seventeen Point Agreement on 23 May 1951'; the Qamdo area was 'placed under the authority of the Qamdo Liberation Committee'.

region.text: U-Tsang (central Tibet), the land of the Seventeen Point Agreement

ledger.note: 23 May 1951: Tibet is annexed by the Seventeen Point Agreement. Infobox territorial change: 'U-Tsang and the Chamdo Region of Kham came under Chinese control'; the Dalai Lama 'formally accepted' the agreement in October 1951 (telegram of 24 October) and 'shortly afterwards, the PLA entered Lhasa' (no date). The Tibetan government 'remained in place' with 'a large degree of autonomy' until the 1959 rising ('the Dalai Lama left Lhasa on March 17') but is not drawn as a vassal because the tibet dossier ends the state in May 1951.

region.text: Aksai Chin, the plateau crossed by the Xinjiang-Tibet road

ledger.note: 1957: China completes a road through Aksai Chin. 'In 1956-57, China constructed a road through Aksai Chin, connecting Xinjiang and Tibet'; after 1962 China 'continued its de facto control of the Aksai Chin'. The page does not date the start of Chinese control; the road's year is the reading and India's claim the reason for the counterpart.

union.text: Aksai Chin, the plateau crossed by the Xinjiang-Tibet road

region.text: Aksai Chin and the North-East Frontier Agency (Arunachal Pradesh)

ledger.note: 20 October 1962: China attacks along the Indian frontier. 'Chinese troops launched an attack on the southern banks of the Namka Chu River on 20 October'; the page places the war in 'Aksai Chin, North-East Frontier Agency, and Assam'.

union.text: Aksai Chin, the plateau crossed by the Xinjiang-Tibet road

region.text: Aksai Chin and the North-East Frontier Agency (Arunachal Pradesh)

ledger.note: 21 November 1962: China declares a ceasefire and withdraws. 'Zhou Enlai declared a unilateral ceasefire to start on midnight, 21 November'; China was to 'withdraw to positions 20 kilometres behind the line of actual control' (the page dates the withdrawal to 1 December 1962); infobox 'Status quo ante bellum'. The ceasefire date differs inside the page (19, 20 or 21 November).

region.text: the strip on the Karakoram watershed added to Cliopatria's 1963 shape beside Aksai Chin

ledger.note: 1963: the China-Pakistan Border Treaty. The page mentions 'a 1963 China-Pakistan Border Treaty' concerning the Pakistan-controlled Kashmir boundary; the strip drawn is the land Cliopatria adds in 1963 on the Karakoram watershed, and the page gives neither its extent nor the date of signing. The islamic-republic-of-pakistan dossier carries the matching loss.

1997: Hong Kong returns to China. The page: the Special Administrative Regions were 'transferred to China in 1997 and 1999 respectively' after the joint declarations 'signed in 1984 and 1987'; Hong Kong is 1,104.4 km2. The page names the former British territory but gives no day. [review ea-08-d 2026-10-25] Month from the Handover of Hong Kong page: the handover 'occurred at midnight on 1 July 1997'.

1999: Macau returns to China. The page: 'transferred to China in 1999' (Macau, 31.3 km2, a former Portuguese territory); no day is given. [review ea-08-d 2026-10-25] Month from the Transfer of sovereignty over Macau page: the handover 'officially occurred at midnight on 20 December 1999'.

wars.name: Chinese Civil War
wars.outcome: Communist victory on the mainland: the Nationalist government left for Taiwan on 7 December 1949, resistance collapsed after Chengdu fell on 10 December 1949 and Hainan fell in April 1950.
wars.note: The war's earlier campaigns are in the communist-party-of-china dossier; this entry is the conquest after the proclamation.

wars.name: Annexation of Tibet by the People's Republic of China

zones.text: the Chamdo Region, the western part of Kham
U-Tsang (central Tibet), the land of the Seventeen Point Agreement

wars.outcome: Chinese victory: Chamdo taken in October 1950; the Seventeen Point Agreement of 23 May 1951, accepted by the Dalai Lama in October 1951, brought U-Tsang and the Chamdo Region under Chinese control.
wars.note: Infobox 6 October 1950 - 24 October 1951. 'Active hostilities were limited to a border area northeast of the Gyamo Ngul Chu River and east of the 96th meridian'; about 2,000 PLA and 2,000 Tibetans killed (PRIO estimate).

wars.name: Sino-Indian War

zones.text: Aksai Chin, the plateau crossed by the Xinjiang-Tibet road

wars.outcome: Chinese victory with 'status quo ante bellum': China kept de facto control of Aksai Chin and withdrew from the North-East Frontier Agency to 20 km behind the line of actual control (1 December 1962).
wars.note: Fought 20 October-21 November 1962; the Namka Chu attack of 20 October, the attack near Chushul of 18 November.

certainty.note: The frontier with India (Aksai Chin, the North-East Frontier Agency) and with the Soviet Union and Burma was unsettled; the page does not date any boundary treaty. The Tibetan frontier of 1950-1951 is the fighting zone east of the 96th meridian.

23 border disputes since 1949, six of them unsettled (China page, closely paraphrased): most land frontiers are treaty lines, but the line of actual control with India stays soft and Hong Kong and Macau are sharp at their 1997 and 1999 transfers. The Taiwan Strait is a coast, not a frontier.

notes: Budget 5 pages, all used (China, Annexation of Tibet, Sino-Indian War, Special administrative regions of China, Chinese Civil War, the last reused from the communist-party-of-china dossier). ONE STATE OR TWO (Q148): two states. The Republic of China (1912-) continues on Taiwan; the People's Republic was proclaimed on 1 October 1949; Q148 on the ROC row is Cliopatria's mistake (the republic-of-china dossier of ea-08-c says the same). The Communist Party of China row (communist-party-of-china) is the pre-state of this one: it dissolves on 1 October 1949 with this state as successor. RAISED FOR THE REVIEWER: (1) Cliopatria's People's Republic starts in 1950; the dossier starts 1 October 1949 with a new keyframe; (2) Hainan is missing from the 1950-1952 shape (April 1950 on the page) and central Tibet is added only in 1953 (the agreement is 23 May 1951): new 1951-1952 keyframe; (3) Aksai Chin is drawn as Chinese from 1957 (road of 1956-57; the war was 'status quo ante bellum') instead of Cliopatria's 1963: confidence 2, the page does not say when control began; (4) the 1963 strip beside Aksai Chin is the Pakistan agreement, explained at confidence 2 because the page only names the treaty; (5) the October-December 1949 conquest of the south and west is one confidence-1 event for the provinces the pages do not date (Xinjiang, Qinghai, Gansu, Yunnan, Guizhou); the three dated cities are separate events. NOT DONE FOR THE PAGE BUDGET (the neighbour dossiers already carry the loss; a gap-filler should open each): the boundary treaties with Burma (1960), Nepal (1961), Mongolia (1962), Pakistan (2 March 1963, in the islamic-republic-of-pakistan ledger), Afghanistan, the Soviet Union (1969 Zhenbao clashes, 1991 agreement), Vietnam (1979 war and the 1999 land border pact, in the socialist-republic-of-vietnam ledger), Kazakhstan (2002), Kyrgyzstan (2009), Tajikistan (2011, 1999 deal), Laos, North Korea (1961 treaty is mentioned on the China page, not described); the Zhoushan and Wanshan islands (May 1950 in the republic-of-china ledger); the Yijiangshan islands and the Taiwan Strait crises (1954-55, 1958); the Paracel Islands (1974) and South China Sea; the Korean War (1950-53) and the PLA in North Korea; the Tibetan rising of March 1959; Xinjiang's 1949 change; the Tibet Autonomous Region (1965). RULERS: no list on the pages. GAZETTEER: no missing names (Hong Kong S.A.R. and Macao S.A.R. resolve; the circle around 79.3 E, 35.0 N (200 km) is a coordinate for Aksai Chin because the gazetteer has only a lake of that name). The matching events of the neighbour dossiers: tibet (occupation of Chamdo October 1950, May 1951 end, dissolve), republic-of-india (contest_start 20 October 1962, contest_end 21 November 1962), republic-of-china (loss of Hainan April 1950, of the mainland from October 1949).
